reason: The contract requires per-component accuracy abs(actual-target) <= 1e-7+5e-7*|target| over the full finite FP16 domain, explicitly including cancellation-heavy small-component cases and subnormal/extreme denominators. Both in-scope failure hypotheses were decisively rebutted: c1 (cancellation-heavy small-component error) by probe t12 covering 699,994 rows including 99,994 targeted near-cancellation rows (d = nearest FP16 to -a*c/b) and uniform samples over ALL finite FP16 values, with zero violations and overall max error/tolerance ratio 0.331; c2 (extreme/subnormal denominator accuracy) by probe t13 covering 509,000 rows including ±65504 extrema, smallest subnormals, zero-mixed and mixed-extreme denominators, with zero violations and max ratio 0.239. Outputs were finite in all batches. Earlier probe failures (t8–t11) were probe-script bugs (indexing and size-cap errors), not kernel behavior, and were superseded by the successful probes. Signed zeros compare equal per contract; the naive FP32 algorithm is contractually permitted since any internal precision is allowed as long as the componentwise tolerance holds, and it demonstrably holds with a large margin (~3x) on the adversarial regions of the stated domain. No confirmed in-scope defect remains; the kernel is correct within the benchmark contract.
